thread.title: PACT cites Florida lawsuit reforms for insurance market gains
thread.title_full: PACT cites Florida lawsuit reforms for insurance market gains

author: E. G. Snowden
title: PACT cites Florida lawsuit reforms for insurance market gains
text:
Protecting American Consumers Together cited Florida’s 2023 tort reforms as an example of how efforts to curb lawsuit abuse can affect insurance markets, citing lower premiums, fewer lawsuits and new insurer entrants.
PACT shared an analysis by Americans for Tax Reform (ATR) that cited Florida’s tort reforms as factors behind 42 insurers filing rate decreases and 15 new companies entering the market. The group said the state has moved from being one of the most heavily litigated insurance markets to seeing broader competition and lower rates following the reforms.
Florida’s 2023 tort reforms under HB 837 reduced the statute of limitations for negligence actions from four years to two years, modified comparative fault and one-way attorney fee provisions, and required greater transparency in medical damages. ATR said the changes were intended to address high levels of insurance-related litigation in the state, including auto glass claims. Before the reforms, Florida accounted for 6% of all U.S. homeowner lawsuits and 99% of all auto glass repair claims.
Following the reforms, property and casualty insurance premiums in Florida decreased by 14.5% overall, with the pace of rate increases slowing significantly, according to the analysis. Auto glass litigation dropped from over 24,000 lawsuits in 2023 to about 2,600 in 2024. Insurance industry legal defense costs fell from $1.6 billion in 2022 to $537 million in 2025. The group also cited 15 new property and casualty insurers entering the market.
PACT is a consumer advocacy organization that focuses on legal reform, litigation practices and consumer protection issues. The group frequently comments on topics related to insurance costs, lawsuit abuse and the civil justice system.
